name: Vladimir Makaroff
bio: A Russian emigre who worked in a London bookshop, and the man Evguenia Souline married after the Second World War, when she was well into her forties - three to six years after Radclyffe Hall's death. He outlived her, and it was his sale of his wife's letters from Hall that put the correspondence into the University of Texas collection where it survives.
bio_note: No dates recorded; Baker describes him only as a Russian emigre working in a London bookshop. Baker's index entry reads 'Makaroff, Vladimir - marriage to Souline 351; sells wife's letters from John 352'. THE HISTORIOGRAPHICAL POINT IS WORTH KEEPING: Baker writes that 'Had not Makaroff sold his wife's letters, which eventually surfaced at the University of Texas, the full story might never have come to light.' The husband is the reason the queer relationship is documented at all.
